# Quillmoor retention: twelve months

The eighteen-month retention for Quillmoor field recordings, set on the 1 October planning call, is replaced by twelve months. The consent renewal letters sent in September came back from fewer than half of the participants, so consent cannot be counted on past the first year. Transcripts are still kept permanently; only the recordings change.

positions.name: ConsentReachForKeptRecordings
positions.frame: How far does participant consent reach when field recordings are kept, and what retention period can it support?
positions.why: The September renewal letters came back from fewer than half of participants, and the statement draws a firm conclusion from that: consent cannot be relied on past the first year. This is a lone statement that bears on the retention rule the settled-facts narrative rests on, so it carries its own frame. It is a survey-based claim with no ratification language, so it does not join the settled-items position. The lineage is 'see' rather than 'extends' because the frame is about consent and does not carry forward the call's settled items.

position_revisions.why: The archive retention rule set on the 2026-10-01 call (eighteen months for raw field recordings, transcripts kept permanently) is no longer current. Recordings now run on a twelve-month term, which replaces the eighteen-month clause. Transcripts are still kept permanently, so that clause survives. src-1 and src-3 together replace the dropped statement, which carried both clauses.

placements.why: Position_PlanningCallSettledItems, as revised, now carries src-1 (the recordings term is replaced by twelve months, so the eighteen-month clause is no longer current) and src-3 (transcripts are still kept permanently). Both are ratified operating facts the team plans against, which is this leaf's subject. ConsentReachForKeptRecordings bears on the retention term the leaf rests on. It is claim-grain rather than ratified, since it draws a firm conclusion from the renewal-letter response rate without recording a settlement. It is placed here as the position pass proposed because it bears directly on the recording term. The leaf already holds the settled-items position, so this placement adds the consent position beside it and does not move anything.
